                                              • From the Biological and Electrical Systems perspective, integrating electrodes into a garment using
                                                conductive textiles (Li et al.) ensures consistent and repeatable placement on the correct dermatomes.
                                                This could significantly improve therapeutic consistency and potentially mitigate the tolerance effect by
                                                ensuring the stimulation is always delivered to the optimal nerve pathways, addressing a key variable
                                                noted in the pain modulation research (Vera-Portocarrero et al.; Vance et al.).

                                              • From the Chemical Systems perspective, our design direction allows us to sidestep the most problematic
                                                components of current TENS technology. By leveraging novel textile-based or dry electrodes (Al-Solihat et
                                                al.; Li et al.), we can move away from the cycle of applying, removing, and replacing disposable hydrogel
                                                electrodes, thereby eliminating the primary source of skin irritation and chemical degradation (Chatterjee
                                                and Inbarani; Lib-It and Ziv-Av).
